headline: Library seeks $1,658,901 FY28 budget and two new full-time positions, an executive assistant and a technician
summary: The library's budget request is $1,658,901, up 1.88% from FY27, with warrant articles for a $20,000 reserve fund and a bond for the next building phase. The acting library director estimated $122,050 a year for the executive assistant and $131,287 for the technician. Other departments presented budgets, including Cable at $316,441 and Public Works solid waste at about 3.9 million.
discussion: Library staffing: The library has 8 full-time and 10 part-time staff. Staff said it is 45 hours a week short of the time needed for its regular work, and shelf reading and inventory are not being done regularly.

Library databases: Members asked about the Hoopla service, which the library will end. Staff said Hoopla cost $1.32 per use in FY26, while Libby costs well under a dollar per use through the consortium.

Recreation needs assessment: The recreation director proposed a third-party needs assessment, about $14,500 in management services. Members asked whether staff could do it, and the director said staff do not have the skills for a study this size.

Recreation staffing: The director asked for a part-time assistant director at 28 hours a week, costing $53,607 a year. The director said the full-time director role now has about 354 fewer budgeted hours a year than the two earlier roles.

Drop-off center fees: Staff said the transfer station fees have not been raised since 1998. Staff said they have only started discussing a new fee schedule, and that the town charges nothing for brush even though its disposal cost has risen.
